chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Sinān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyyah, who said:

When you bring your brother to the grave, do not place him into it abruptly. Set him down below the grave by two or three cubits so that he may take his preparation; then place him in his niche, press his cheek to the earth, uncover his face, and let the one most entitled among the people to him stand at the side of his head. Then let him recite the Opening of the Book.
And the two refuge-seeking surahs and Āyat al-Kursī; then let him say whatever he knows until he finishes with his companion.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: the Throne Verse, recited here as part of burial recitation
key_terms.أُهْبَتَهُ: his preparation or readiness before being placed fully into the grave
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave into which the deceased is brought for burial
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: the two surahs of seeking refuge, Sūrat al-Falaq and Sūrat al-Nās
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: his companion, meaning the deceased person being buried
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, recited at the graveside
key_terms.لَحْدِهِ: his burial niche cut into the side of the grave

ai.seo_question: What should be recited and done when placing a deceased person into the grave in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of placing the deceased into the grave and the recitations to be made at burial. It presents recommended burial etiquette, including gentleness with the deceased, positioning in the laḥd, and recitation of Qur'anic passages at the graveside.
